mainText:
Dairy prices have risen for a third consecutive Global Dairy Trade auction, while the All Blacks prepare for Scotland in Edinburgh after the sudden death of their long serving security chief.

New Zealand.

Global Dairy Trade prices rose three percent overnight, the second straight auction increase, with whole milk powder up five point nine percent. New Zealand dairy production has also reached a record high, with milksolids up four point five percent and artificial breeding at a three decade high. Nicola Willis says a left wing coalition would be a, quote, jambalaya of a government. The final 1News Verian poll before Saturday's election shows National and Labour both gaining support, while ACT and New Zealand First have lost ground. Winston Peters has called the campaign the worst he has seen and a circus, pointing to an Electoral Commission issue with enrolment eligibility for people on residence class visas. Early voting has passed one million, with nearly one hundred and sixty thousand people voting on Monday alone. Police are investigating businessman Harry Mowbray's Split Your Vote website, which urges National supporters to split their ballot. My Food Bag will stay listed on the NZX after a strategic review found no buyer, following market testing of investors in New Zealand and overseas. Revolut has become New Zealand's twenty seventh bank and the first digital only bank, after gaining Reserve Bank registration.

In Western Bay of Plenty, councillor Alan Kurtovich has resigned over the council's Māori wards decision, triggering a byelection. A man who stabbed a friend to death after a party, Dallas Hohua, has had his sentence reduced and may serve as little as two years for manslaughter.

World.

Commonwealth leaders have opened the summit in Antigua and Barbuda. King Charles called climate change the crisis of our time and described the slave trade as a shameful chapter, stopping short of an apology Caribbean nations are demanding. Russian strikes killed at least thirty eight people in Ukraine in twenty four hours, hitting an aid centre, a hospice and a hospital. President Zelensky has warned dozens more may be trapped under rubble. Americans are voting in midterm elections that will decide control of Congress. Severe weather, including flash floods and tornadoes, has disrupted polling in several states. A Learjet crash in South Florida killed nine people, including a technology entrepreneur and his family. North Korea has denied involvement in the six point three billion US dollar Binance hack, which Binance says involved fake job interviews used to target an engineer. Two analytics firms have linked the hack to a North Korean group. Users have withdrawn three point six billion US dollars from the exchange since the breach. A cyber attack has also hit supermarket freezers across ten European countries, pushing temperatures as high as fifty degrees and forcing retailers to dump spoiled food.

Technology.

Alphabet has lost about five hundred billion US dollars in market value after revealing its own artificial intelligence search summaries are cutting into advertising revenue, sending the stock to a six month low. It is part of a wider sell off, with the Nasdaq at its lowest level in more than two months as investors question whether nearly one trillion US dollars in artificial intelligence spending is matched by returns. Intel shares have continued falling. Anthropic is preparing a possible listing on the Nasdaq, with New Zealand brokerage Sharesies among those planning to let local investors take part.

Sport.

Rugby league. The Kiwis have named their side for the Rugby League World Cup semifinal against Tonga, with Ponga returning. Forward Jacob Laban remains out through injury and misses the rest of the tournament. The Kiwi Ferns have also named their side, for their semifinal against Samoa.

All Blacks. Head of security Logan Cadwallader has died in Edinburgh after a medical event, ahead of Saturday's test against Scotland at Murrayfield. Assistant coach Jason Ryan says the squad is heartbroken but will pick its strongest possible side, calling it the toughest of weeks before facing a Scotland team that pushed them all the way last year.

Netball. Ali Williams has ruled out a rebel league after his and Anna Mowbray's proposed privatised competition deal with Netball New Zealand fell through. The Waikato Bay of Plenty Magic says the model would have been out of reach for at least one existing franchise, leaving players facing months of uncertainty over their professional futures.

Golf. Ryan Fox will play in the World Tour finale in Dubai despite safety concerns raised over the Middle East conflict affecting the season ending tournaments in Abu Dhabi and Dubai.

Cricket. Devon Conway is out of the one day international against India after a head clash with Matt Henry at training on Tuesday. Coach Rob Walter is managing a squad already stretched by injuries.

Youth Olympics. New Zealand swimmer Ariel Muchirahondo has won a second gold, taking the one hundred metres backstroke after already winning the two hundred metres backstroke.

Coming up. The Kiwis play Tonga and the Kiwi Ferns play Samoa in Rugby League World Cup semifinals this week. The All Blacks play Scotland at Murrayfield on Saturday. Election day is Saturday the seventh of November.

End of flash.
